title: QBR Activation→Renewal Playbook & Slide Bank (Standard + Enterprise)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc is a working playbook + slide bank for QBRs that explicitly ties activation signals to renewal outcomes. It includes:
- a compact slide-by-slide template for Standard (SMB / mid-market) and Enterprise QBRs,
- an operational renewal-risk tracker CSV schema and example rows,
- playbook steps for pre-QBR prep, during the meeting, and post-QBR follow ups,
- enterprise-specific negotiation and procurement checkpoints,
- suggested speaker notes and data calls.

Why this variant?
Most existing QBR decks are organized around usage and outcomes. This version is built to:
1) surface the activation events that predict renewal (first API call patterns, latency targets met, initial integrations live) and connect them directly to topics in the QBR;
2) provide a concise renewal risk tracker that the CSM, AE, and Solutions Eng can co-own;
3) add enterprise gating/checklists (SLA requests, legal/SC signature timeline, procurement PO cadence) so the team can preempt renewal friction.

Audience:
- Primary: CSMs running customer QBRs (SMB / mid-market)
- Variant: CSM + AE + Solutions lead for Enterprise accounts

Template constraints (how to use):
- Keep Standard QBR to 30–35 minutes; Enterprise QBR to 45–60 minutes.
- Slide count: Standard 8–12, Enterprise 12–18.
- Start with health and activation story (not raw usage). Charts should be annotated with the event-level drivers.
- Use the Renewal Risk Tracker export as the single source-of-truth before the meeting (do not paste multiple tables into slides).

Slide-by-slide (Standard QBR, ~30 min):
1) Title + one-line objective (1 slide)
   - Objective examples: "Sync: confirm value delivered and align on next 90d plan"
   - Speaker note: set expectations (time, who owns follow-ups).
2) Quick wins snapshot (1 slide)
   - 3 bullet outcomes since last call (Activation events: 1st embed, model pinned, latency < target)
3) Health snapshot (1 slide)
   - Metrics: health_score (0–100), NRR proxy (usage delta), support escalations open, MTTR trend
   - Visual: compact sparkline + current value callout
4) Activation timeline (1 slide)
   - Show first 90 days funnel: sign-up → dev API call → production request → integrated feature live
   - Callout: conversion rates at each step and time-to-integrate median
5) Feature adoption map (1 slide)
   - Top 3 features used (embeddings, rerank, streaming) + top 2 suppressed features
6) Cost & utilization memo (1 slide)
   - Effective cost per 1k tokens, reserved vs burst usage, recommendation if applicable (batching/quantization)
7) Risk signals & recommended mitigations (1 slide)
   - Derived from the Renewal Risk Tracker (see below)
8) Ask / roadmap alignment (1 slide)
   - Concrete asks: test dataset for Optimize evals, permission to trial dedicated capacity, timing for procurement
9) Next steps & owners (1 slide)
   - 3 follow-ups with owner and target date

Enterprise QBR additions (use after slide 4, expand to 12–18 slides):
- Procurement & procurement timeline (PO, contract amendments)
- SLA/Latency pledges and current telemetry with 95/99 percentiles
- Security & compliance updates (audit log access, KMS integration status)
- Integration health matrix (SI contact, tenant isolation, network tests)
- Commercial scenarios: upsell triggers and discount renewal windows

Renewal Risk Tracker (CSV schema - single-line header):
customer,account_owner,ae,cs_owner,arr,term_end,health_score,last_activity_date,last_solution_deploy,activation_events,open_blockers,legal_status,procurement_status,next_renewal_engagement,date_of_last_meeting,renewal_risk_level,notes

Sample rows (CSV lines):
Acme Corp,Jordan Lee,Jordan Lee,Nina Patel,225000,2026-06-30,86,2026-01-12,2025-12-15,"api_integration,low_latency",none,completed,po_requested,2026-02-10,low,"Expanding to two more teams Q2"
Borealis Inc,Carmen Ruiz,Jordan Lee,Lina Zhao,480000,2026-04-30,62,2025-12-04,2025-12-02,"trial_dropped,patch_pending",security_review_pending,contract_review,procurement_blocked,2026-01-15,high,"Legal has 2 redlines; AE aligned to escalate"

How to score renewal_risk_level (quick rubric):
- low: health_score > 75 AND no open blockers AND procurement/contract clear
- medium: health_score 50–75 OR 1 moderate blocker or delayed procurement
- high: health_score < 50 OR unresolved security/legal issues OR customer hasn't used product in 4+ weeks

Pre-QBR checklist (timeline):
- 21 days: export Renewal Risk Tracker, verify fields, assign owners for red/high rows (CS + AE + SE).
- 14 days: data-check call between CS and SE: confirm activation_events are reproducible and up-to-date.
- 7 days: draft deck + internal review comments (send to AE and Solutions).
- 3 days: practice run for Enterprise accounts (run-through with AE + SE).
- 1 day: send final deck + agenda + pre-read (attach short CSV of top 5 renewal-risk accounts if multi-customer QBR review).

During the meeting (facilitation script - high level):
- 0–3 min: introduce attendees, objectives, and success criteria for this QBR.
- 3–10 min: articulate activation story and Quick Wins. Avoid showing raw logs — show impact.
- 10–18 min: health snapshot + key metrics; highlight one anomaly and the corrective plan.
- 18–25 min: roadmap alignment & asks. For Enterprise, include SLA/procurement slide here.
- Final 5 min: commitments (owner + date). Write them to the tracker live.

Post-QBR playbook (immediately after call):
- 24 hours: send meeting notes + action tracker with owners and due dates.
- 72 hours: AE and CS confirm procurement/contract follow ups. If high risk, bring in Solutions Eng and RevOps for escalation.
- 7 days: update Renewal Risk Tracker to reflect mitigations; call out any change in risk_level.

Enterprise negotiation checklist (practical):
- Confirm renewal timeline against legal review cycles (add buffer for external procurement: 4–6 weeks).
- Pre-fill the SOW language for feature usage caps and SLA credits to avoid back-and-forth.
- Map internal signatories (Procurement, IT Security, Legal) and track their expected decision dates in the tracker.
- Offer short pilot extension (30 days) with clear success criteria if procurement stalls.

Loose speaker notes (copyable soundbites):
- "Since we last met, we saw the dev-to-prod conversion go from 22% → 41% — that directly drove a 18% increase in query volume which translates to X revenue impact; we want to repeat that pattern in two additional teams."
- "Our health score components are reliability (40%), usage (30%), support (20%), and roadmap alignment (10%) — here's why reliability ticked down this quarter and how we fixed it."
- "For enterprise renewal cadence: we want procurement signoff 45 days before term_end; if we don't have PO in hand by day -30 we trigger a weekly procurement check-in with the AE and RevOps."

Common objections + quick responses:
- "We can't commit to more spend until integration stabilizes." → "Let's run a targeted Optimize study to quantify unit-cost improvements and commit to a 30-day trial of batching/quantization changes."
- "Legal needs tighter data residency terms." → "We can propose an addendum and offer a private deployment checklist; we'll route to Private Sales and Solutions for scoping within 48 hours."

Deck hygiene checklist (before sending):
- Remove raw query logs; include only aggregated metrics and annotated charts.
- Add one-line action items on the final slide with owners.
- Replace placeholder screenshots with production telemetry screenshots (with dates).

Appendix (helpful snippets):
- Data call templates for Engineering: "Please confirm last successful full integration test and share any open support tickets referencing integration failures (ticket ids)."
- Short email template for follow-up (one-paragraph): "Thanks for the QBR — attached are the notes and agreed next steps. Owner X is tracking Y and we’ll follow up by DATE."

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Add a short one-slide deep-dive template for "cost-per-1000 tokens" that pulls in estimated GPU minutes, average seq_len, and quantization tier (action: Lina).
- Build a script to export Renewal Risk Tracker from Gainsight / internal dashboards (action: Carlos).
- Create a one-click deck generator that maps tracker rows to slides for account bundles (longer-term product ask).

Action items (owner + ETA):
- Lina Zhao: draft cost deep-dive slide (ETA: 2026-02-28)
- Carlos Gutierrez: prototype tracker export (ETA: 2026-03-10)
- Priya Menon: test enterprise pre-read pack with AE (ETA: 2026-03-05)

Status notes: this is a working draft — please comment inline. The goal is to converge on a concise standard QBR that CSMs can run in 30 minutes while having the Enterprise version include the procurement/legal checkpoints that traditionally cause last-minute renewal risk.
